title: I need some help with dosing
body:
A little backstory: I have extreme chronic pain, and where I live pain medicine is controlled and so there are no doctors who will prescribe me anything for pain, which is frustrating. 
Anyway, I found a guy who has been selling me percocets for the last 6 months and I have been taking about 6 a day, sometimes more depending on how bad my pain is. The guy who provided them doesn't have anymore at the moment and I am suffering from withdrawals. The guy gave me Suboxone and said it helps with withdrawals, but the thing is he said he has no idea how much or how often I should take them and because this is the first time I have heard of this stuff, I'm kind of afraid of taking them especially since I don't know how much to take or how often to take them. 

So my questions are, what's the starting dose of this stuff? How often should I take them? How do I ingest it, do I swallow them? I thought I read somewhere you put them under your tongue, is this true? He gave me 2mg and 8 mg pills. Is that too much or too little? How long after my last percocet dose should I take it? My last percocet dose was 18 hours ago and I feel awful, and it will only get worse, right?  
I'm so torn on what to do. On one hand I want this crappy feeling to go away now, but on the other hand I'm too afraid to take something foreign to me that has never been prescribed. 

Not only do I have lots of questions about Suboxone, but I'm also looking for support. I'm just really scared right now because I feel like I'm dying.
comment:
If you were taking 30mg of OC a day, I probably start with just the 2mg pill.
It's taken sublingually. Hold it under your tongue until it dissolves. I usually hold the liquid in my mouth for 10 min after it dissolves then swallow it. 
Wait an hour. If you're not feeling relief, take another mg or two. I don't think you will need over 4mg a day. 
You may need to redose in 12 hours. You'll eventually figure out what works for you.
You don't want to over do it because taking too much can make you sick. 
Sub has an extremely long half life.

title: The spit method
body:
I just started on 4 mg subs cycle yesterday as a way to exit a very heavy (80-100 gpd) and very long term (8 years) kratom cycle. First time user of subs. So far so good. 

I do not intend to be on subs very long. Maybe 12 or so days. Perhaps a bit longer. Will have to see how it pans out. I just want to use subs to get through the kratom CT acutes and paws that I am oh so familiar with. Trust me, I am very well versed when it comes to CT from very high doses. It sucks and I am not usually successful at all muscling my way through a taper. But I digress...

I’ve been reading about the spit method to avoid the Naloxone side effects such as headache and/or vision issues. How much buprenorphine is lost if the remaining liquid is spit out from mouth after tab is fully dissolved? Is it negligible?
comment:
While relapse is likely, to say "you ARE going to relapse" is a bit far fetched. Yea it is likely but if you have the correct mindset and this is absolutely what you want to do then go for it. That said, I personally think long term maintenance is the better option. Get on subs, stay on them for a while, get your life in order, begin a long slow taper. Just my opinion. Whatever you decide good luck to you and let us know how it goes. 

Oh, and if you spit it out after dissolving for 30 minutes or more you are not losing anything. I spit mine out sometimes after dissolving for 30-60 minutes.

title: Why do you really want to quit subs?
body:
I’m not judging nor being accusatory but why do you personally truly want to be off of Subs. At one point in time they were a lifesaver to stop the damage and cycle of addiction. Lately I’ve been stabilizing but here were some thoughts that have entered my mind on why I would like to eventually come off of them. 

* The other night I was just feeling “meh”. Not up , not down. I’m not used to not being able to manipulate my body to feel a certain way. Made me feel trapped. Kind of depressed. Then the next morning I woke up and went to work and was glad I was on them and couldn’t use. 

* What if I could just be off of them. Then I wouldn’t need to be on something every day. Then I remembered how I felt the other night and am convinced I would have used “something” to feel better.

* I miss the highs. How do I ever capture that overwhelming feeling of positivity, peace (at that moment) and sociable person. A life without highs? Fuck. 

* How am I supposed to deal with these social events coming up. I don’t know who I am without manipulating my personality before entering these situations. I feel helpless at times not being able to manipulate my feelings to cope with “x” scenario. 

* Where the fuck is my reward after a hard work day 

* I’m just normal on them. I’ve never been normal. How is this a good life to live ? Life seems to mundane. I can’t alter myself. This is strange. 

So these are reasons in my head (fleeting but I’m just being real) of why I can see myself getting off subs. Not to say I would go use again but on subs we are all kind of maxed out on what we can feel. I’m not used to that and haven’t been in over a decade. 

Anyone else help share some reasons why you truly want off of subs. Are all of you just wanting off to be off of taking a substance or can anyone relate to what I’ve felt above? 

Thanks.
comment:
1. I just knew I had to finally pull the band aid off. If I ran out of subs I would feel like I was chasing the dope man like I was still a fiend, literally no different and it was depressing.
2. The feeling of taking something and feeling like I just threw on armor and a sword and was ready for anything was gone and had been gone for a long time.
3. Pretty sure they crashed my endocrine system, could still get a boner and have a sex drive. But I literally just felt like shit with no energy and had no interest in the opposite sex. A chick would want to come over and I'd just beat off and go to sleep instead. Made my legs kick and made me jump out of my sleep, memory problems, headaches, vertigo. So I figure they're probably not good for brain health long term.
4. I know if I got sent to some island without subs or any drugs I would find a way to survive, I wouldn't lay there screaming for subs and dope. Therefore these things saving me the rest of my life from impending doom is just my imagination.
5. I haven't gotten high on opiates in years, but I'm taking something that's bad for me in the end so I don't do something else I don't even want to do. Subs became my drug of choice and I felt it was ridiculous.
6. Just overall mental health, spirituality, mental clarity, whatever you want to call it. I would be pissed all the time over stupid shit, and would literally be yelling at people in my head like a lunatic on a daily basis. I hardly had a real belly laugh in years and just felt overall dread majority of the time with no connection to the people around me. Worked on stuff for years, tried to work on me and it was just process of elimination in the end.

title: Using pain killers to get off suboxone?
body: So. This is going to sound weird, but I actually wasn’t put on suboxone for opiate dependence. I was put on it 3 years ago because this new age doctor said it could help with my depression by raising my dopamine levels. Anyways long story short. 3 years later I am on testosterone therapy at 28. Because the suboxone killed my T levels so much. My libido/mood/energy/etc is still super up or down even with testosterone therapy. My hormone doctor says that getting off the suboxone would help immensely in making the testosterone work better. I want to get off the suboxone but I heard it’s worse then opiate withdrawals. Which I have no idea what those are like, but I have heard they are miserable. And I have also heard suboxone withdrawals last longer. I guess my question is, could I stop the suboxone for maybe 3 days. Switch to maybe something like Percocet or Vicodin. Stay on those for maybe 2 months. And by the time the 2 months has passed the suboxone should be totally out of my system and then just stop the painkillers? I know this sounds crazy and stupid. But just wondering if it’s an option. I feel trapped on this drug. I just feel numb to life at times and I honestly feel like I felt better before I went on it. Thanks for any help. I heard reddit is a pretty good place for opioid help!
comment:
Holy shit, that new age doctor should lose his/her licence. That's really fucked up and I'm sorry you have to go through this because your dr. thought it will help you with your dopamine levels. I've never heard such a stupid reason for Suboxone treatment and it's definitely not something that probably any doctor would do in a similar situation. There are far less addictive alternatives for that, like bupropion or even l-thyrosine. Buprenorphine is totally wrong drug for correcting low dopamine levels.

I have no experience of switching buprenorphine to something that has shorter half-life but in theory, that could work. You have to keep in mind that full-agonist opioids (which you were thinking) are far more addictive than Suboxone and usually this goes another way around, so you have to be extremely cautious. Always take only what you need and try to tolerate minor withdrawls. You can't do it without feeling any WD's but with right choices you can make it manageable.

Good luck and fuck that quack doctor!

title: Day 23 update - please read if you're wanting to get off
body:
~preface~

Abused oxy for 2.5 years, started with small amounts but towards the end of it was using 200-300 mg most days. Then got on subs for 4 months. Tapered from 8 mg to 0.5ish. I felt good starting subs, and the taper was easy enough for the first couple months. Then the last month, under 1mg, I found myself hating the negative side effects and was just ready to be sober. I read so so so much about the withdrawals and stuff that I was really scared to jump. But at the same time I was just always in a bad mood, no energy, sex drive, feelings. I couldn't take being on subs anymore. So I got my affairs in order, told my dr, took a week off work, went out of town so I wasn't tempted and just fucking jumped. 

the jump & honeymoon phase~

The first few days following my jump, I constantly felt like it was right about hit me. That at any moment the real opiate wds were about to start. Body temp regulation was a bit off, mild RLS at night, insomnia - but nothing terrible at this point. After another few days of laziness I realized it wasn't going to fuck my shit up like I thought it would. In fact, I started feeling better!.  Got goosebumps from books, vibed to music, and cried from movies. Reached out to old friends I hadn't talked to in a while. My appetite came back with a vengeance. FOOD IS SO GOOD AGAIN. Suffer knowing the end is near and life will be soso much improved should help get through the tough parts. I ate like a beast. I can concentrate on things relatively easy. Sex is sex again.

~paws~

The mild withdrawals lasted about a week. Despite them I felt damn good having feelings and energy again even without getting much sleep. Then that chapter ended and a new one began. This one was different, I felt no physical withdrawals but the mental component was a struggle. Depression, lethargy, a bit anxiety - but still better than when I was on 0.5g subs. This was worst around day 10. However day by day, I began slowly building myself back up. Starting running, and noticed I felt much better after doing exercise. Kept eating healthy and taking care of my body. Kept staying busy with books and movies. Each day has been better and better. I'm now at day 23 and feel more like my old self than ever before. Still struggling a bit with sleep and energy but overall feel good and proud of myself for NOT being dependent on any god damn substance or medicine to feel okay for the first time in years. Totally worth it

To anyone fretting about jumping - 

I can't promise you that your experience will be like mine. Everyone is different, and that especially applies to sub metabolism. But please, please, please just trust yourself, your doctor's, and your loved ones that support you. Don't believe all the horror stories from reddit. It'll be over before you realize it. And it always does get better!!!!!

comment:
If any of your H was cut with fentanyl then you're looking at a longer time between last use of it and then starting suboxone. Obviously hold out for as long as you can mentally, but know that inducing subs too early and triggering precipitated withdrawal will make you feel 1000 times worse. Pure hell on earth. 

Once you've waited enough time and want to start just start with ~0.5mg just so if there are still opiates on your brain's receptors then the PWD won't be too to bad. After an hour of your first dose you don't feel any relief or PWD then you can start increasing doses ~1-2mg at a time. You can always take more, not less. 

Buprenorphine doesn't get an opioid dependent user high but it's still one of the strongest opioids out there. 
If you're not careful it will cause a lot of harm. Stay safe!

comment:
I have so many comments to make, but I gotta go to work...

1. Don't snort zubsolv!! Thr naloxone is way more bioavailable up the nose. Naloxone can't be absorbed sublingually. That's why the films and tablets are all sublingual. If swallowed, you can get a little bit of naloxone through the stomach. 

Snorted = way more naloxone in the blood stream.  That's why they have a narcan nasal spray.

Narcan = shot or nasal spray.

So, soaking a suboxone strip and shooting it, or crushing and sniffing a tablet with naloxone in it = narcan'ing yourself.

Stick with sublingual, that way you get your meds into your system and NOT the narcan.

2. The dosing strength on zubsolv is a different number because it's a different compound. The zubsolv 5.7 has the same amount of buprenorphine as an 8-2mg suboxone strip.

Zubsolv comes in a wider variety of strengths because it was designed with a taper in mind. There are more steps in the taper because it's way harder to cut tablets than the strips.

3. Subutex isn't available in the US anymore. There is a generic version, that's just a buprenorphine only sublingual tablet. No naloxone.

The recommendation is that it's only for pregnant or breastfeeding women. It's getting harder and harder to write for it, so many pharmacies giving us hassles and shit.

It's going to continue to get harder to get. 

The only reason it exists for pregnant women is to create a failsafe in the case of abuse (sniffing or shooting).  The naloxone that becomes bioavailable when you snort or inject it = instant withdrawal.   Someone dependent on opioids who goes into immediate withdrawal, could jeopardize a fetus. The stress of withdrawal could kill a baby. 

So, they allow pregnant women access to the version without naloxone, so just in case, if a pg women decides to crush and snort or soak and shoot her meds (instead of taking "as directed"), the baby won't be at risk. 

4. The generic suboxone strips are not cheaper for everyone. Where I live and work, most insurance companies have made deals with indivior and suboxone the brand is the covered formulary choice, thus the generic strips are not covered and are costing way more.

Editing every single script to say "DAW brand name suboxone" has been a giant pain in thr ass.

It's so fucked up that these insurance companies and the pharmaceutical companies are making so much money off us, and making everything so fucking difficult and complicated. Ugh.

5. Some people looooove suboxone. Some people swear that zubsolv is the best. Some people do the generic bup-nal tablets and say they're great.

Everyone is different. Every single human has such a variety in metabolic factors.... It's so impossible to know if you'd respond to a med the same way as anyone else.

We do genetic testing to help shed light on a lot of metabolic factors that affect how you absorb / respond to substances.  Humans are so fucking different, there is so much variety, it's a miracle to me that any product exists for mass consumption. We all respond to substances soooo differently.

Most people who switch from one version of a bup-nal to another, do just fine. Some people have an adjustment period of a few weeks.

Just make sure you're taking whatever version you're on, as directed, to try and maximize your buprenorphine absorption.

There are a ton of tips on reddit about like drying your mouth out and not swallowing your spit, etc. You want as much to get absorbed sublingually, as possible. 

6. Good luck, op and everyone else on meds!!!

I said I hoped he had plenty of non-narcotic arrows in his quiver because I did not want to wake up in surgery (I didn't)!

That night, after surgery and post-op, back in my room, they injected morphine (don't know how much) and were giving me 2 x 10mg Percosette every 4 hours. Nothing. It was a long night. Kind of got off track but my point is, at least for me, switching from Suboxone to Zubsolv  to the orange tablets then back to Zubsolv never bothered me, other than a mild headache the first day they switched me to the orange tablets. title: Does anyone know how long it takes from the last time you took suboxone until withdrawals kick in?
body: I take 16 mg a day for reference.
comment:
If you mean from taking your normal dose daily, to a dead cold stop, no taper, then the half-life will play out over 12 to 36 hours, depending on your dosage, length of time taking, metabolism, etc. 
That being said, the psychological withdrawals can be immediate, for some people. Like me. First time I stopped, didn’t want to, just ran out and was far away from doctors, I was fucking hurting the same day, pure mental. At 16mg per day, I’d strongly recommend tapering out for as far and long as possible, maybe even “aerobraking” if you have some left, which is basically stop taking until you’re hurting, hold out as long as possible, then longer, then take 2mg, or even less. It’s possible you don’t need 16mg, and this method will help resetting your dose way lower, then you taper down from that. Second time I stopped I was on 16mg also, but only had 12 pills, aero’d down to 2mg, then tapered from that over the next 4 months, made a world of difference.

title: Tapering with liquid?
body: I see a lot of people who jump from very low numbers under .25 etc. I was wondering if it would be a good idea to take a 60ml bottle and dilute my strips into it and dose by drops. I'm prescribed 8mg but I'm down to 2-3mg a day. If it is effective, how can i measure it out per drop,?
comment:
I started doing this about 20 days ago.  What I did:

1.  Took 1 x 8mg pill, crushed to fine powder (I cant get strips, but they dissolve the same.)

2.  Tool a 30ml dropper bottle with a 1ml dropper with measurements printed on the dropper. (1 dropper = 1ml)

3.  Mixed 3:1 Propylene Glycol and distilled water for a total of 30+/- ml liquid mixture total.

4.  Mixed in the suboxone powder.  Shake vigorously.

With this method you can slowly titrate by single drops at a time if you choose to.  You can always change the potency as well by using less than 30ml liquid, but I wouldn't recommend it. (Personal preference)

title: Hard to Wrap My Head Around
body:
I began MAT to assist with my stepping out of pain management with oxy/hydro after almost 11 years. As well, I needed to find a solution to address my chronic pain (Multiple Sclerosis/Broken Neck). 

I didn’t expect the pain relief to be as good as it is. My initial plan to stay in MAT for 90 days and then taper while searching out pain solutions. 

It’s now hitting home with me that Suboxone may be with me for a very long time as it works so well. I’m grateful, but I’m also anxious by the thought of being dependent, which we all know has or will happen (85 days on).

I wanted to stop the other drugs being prescribed by pain management because they weren’t working any longer and I was simply over the monthly hassle of going through the PM gauntlet. 

The MAT visits are so easy and simple and I don’t feel on guard all the time. But still, it’s hard for me to think/know Suboxone may be the rest of my life answer for me.

Anyone else using Subs for PM and experience anxiety about being dependent to keep your life moving forward?

I  think something that may be impacting my anxiety is that I’ve had the crap scared out of me by reading some Redditor’s posts about the hell they’ve experienced while tapering and let’s not forget the fear that sits under the surface of “What if I’m in a bad accident.”   

I’m not sure what it will take to decrease my anxiety surrounding Suboxone for life. All I know is I’m feeling tremendously better... pain is controlled, so I’m checked in and present. This is a lovely state to live in a compared to going to PM just to stay out of withdrawal. 

Pearls of wisdom anyone?

Remember that we are all different, and our reactions will be different, although similar in ways. IMO, Suboxone is a life-saving medication; it treats addiction and treats pain, depression, and anxiety in some of us. If it's working for you and you are comfortable with your treatment plan, don't let others influence you into making a decision that may not be the right path for you. I've been on Suboxone for five years now, and I don't fear being on Suboxone long-term or even the rest of my life. I fear what life would be like if it weren't an option. I hope that helps... Best wishes and hugs!
